purpose: Fixture coverage annotations only. API registration and retained metadata do not establish native execution or Terraform lifecycle support.
verification_artifact: The command creates a private owned workspace and report.json. Only completed stages enter the report. Strict refresh-only exit 2 with no resource drift, resource changes or changed output actions is retained with its exact plan and JSON. Independent stages and ordinary destroy still run, but the final status remains failed. No nonzero no-op is accepted.
fixture_consumers: Signed S3 producer writes actual partitioned JSON source rows.
Trino executes saved SELECT and workgroup-scoped prepared EXECUTE. Separate signed SDK and S3 clients read paginated rows and result-object bytes.
Trino executes partitioned Hive Parquet CTAS and INSERT. Independent S3 reads validate actual Parquet objects and manifest bytes. Independent SELECT reads the written rows.
Kafka-backed Kinesis PutRecord is consumed by both GetRecords and the Terraform registered SubscribeToShard consumer.
Firehose DirectPut and KinesisStreamAsSource deliver actual bytes into separate S3 prefixes. Revision 2 changes delivery compression to GZIP.
Optional --glue-job executes a real Python-shell container and consumes its S3 output. The option fails when either required installed Glue image is absent; it does not skip execution.

Native Spark typed DropNamespace projection drives actual Glue-owned DROP DATABASE RESTRICT/CASCADE/IF EXISTS. Independent real Glue reads verify metadata absence and actual S3 bytes remain unchanged.

The fixture records only observed null-to-empty provider collection projections and exact separately managed IAM inline-policy or Glue partition-index contents in one inspected refresh-only creation plan. Parent identity, full policy/index values and active index status must match the separately managed resources. Any other drift fails. It requires strict no-op refresh and plans. The known core exit 2 without semantic changes remains a final failure, not a passing assertion.

The same owned SQLite database is reopened after update. Fresh Trino reads consume retained JSON and Parquet rows; original CTAS/INSERT manifests and Parquet hashes must be unchanged. Kinesis reads the prior native sequence and bytes, Firehose S3 hashes must be unchanged, and fresh standard/enhanced consumers and delivery run again.

docs_update.service_fix: Athena BatchGetNamedQuery now loads typed named queries and checks the current IAM workgroup authority for each requested ID. It returns ordinary per-ID unprocessed errors for missing or denied entries and rejects batches outside 1..50. Current-provider named-query data sources can use the real batch read.
docs_update.drop_database_fix: Spark's typed namespace deletion plan retains IfExists and Cascade. Athena forwards deletion to a Glue-owned atomic RESTRICT check and metadata cascade under the existing current IAM/API-event transaction. Public Glue DeleteDatabase still cascades. IF EXISTS suppresses missing-database errors, not current authorization failures.
docs_update.recent_behavior_preserved: The fixture consumes existing native Hive CTAS/INSERT manifests and calibrated Glue absent-statistics deletion without changing those owners.
docs_update.fixture_fixes: Declare the real STANDARD job class, retain strict core refresh failures without passing them, save exact Terraform command logs, and verify retained plus fresh native consumers after controller reopen.
docs_update.catalog_update_fix: Athena UpdateDataCatalog preserves omitted Parameters and Description. Supplied parameters replace the old map. The resulting catalog still passes type-specific validation under the existing current IAM, tag and transaction boundary. Rejected changes leave the real catalog unchanged.
